class.name: LandscapeSpline3D
class.brief_description: A road, river or stream laid along a spline over a [Landscape3D].
class.description: [LandscapeSpline3D] sweeps a strip of mesh [member width] meters wide along its [member Path3D.curve] and renders it with [member material]. The strip can drape over the [Landscape3D] it sits on ([member height_mode]), and the spline can shape that landscape to itself: cut and fill the ground under a road to the curve's height, dig a bed for a river, and paint a [TerrainLayer] underneath (see [method apply_to_landscape]). Being a [Path3D], its curve is drawn and edited with the ordinary Path3D tools in the 3D editor's toolbar. Turn on their [b]Snap to Colliders[/b] option to drop new points straight onto the terrain, or place them roughly and use [b]Snap Points to Terrain[/b] from this node's own toolbar. Points left without handles are joined smoothly (see [member smooth]), so a road can be laid by clicking along its route. [member spline_type] picks between a road, a river and a stream; changing it in the Inspector also sets the rest of the properties to suit that type (see [method get_preset]). The spline finds its landscape by itself when it is a descendant of the [Landscape3D], or when the landscape is a direct child of one of the spline's ancestors (for example [code]World/Landscape3D[/code] next to [code]World/Roads/MainRoad[/code]); otherwise, set [member landscape_path]. A spline can cross an entire terrain, so it is built not to cost as much as one: - The strip is split into chunks of about [member chunk_length] along the spline, each a separate instance with its own bounds, so frustum and occlusion culling skip the parts out of view, and mesh level of detail (which the renderer chooses per instance, from the distance to its bounds) coarsens the distant parts rather than the whole strip being drawn as finely as its nearest point. - Every chunk is simplified before it is built: cross-sections, and columns across the width, that lie within [member simplify_tolerance] of the surface their neighbors already describe are dropped, so straight and even stretches cost a handful of triangles however finely [member segment_length] samples them. Each chunk also gets its own level of detail meshes, whose switching thresholds are the measured distance between each coarser surface and the full one. - Only what changes is rebuilt: moving a point, or sculpting the terrain under part of the spline (the landscape reports what it changed through [signal Landscape3D.terrain_changed]), rebuilds just the chunks affected, and those are built on worker threads in parallel. Changes made within one frame are gathered into a single update at the end of it. - Vertex data is stored compressed, and by default the strip casts no shadows ([member cast_shadow]), since something lying on the ground has nothing to shadow and would otherwise be drawn once more for every shadow cascade. When [member material] is empty, the spline renders with a built-in material for its [member spline_type]: an asphalt road with shoulders, or water that flows along the spline (from its first point to its last), darkens with depth and fades out at its shoreline. [method create_default_material] makes an editable copy of it. Both built-in materials nudge the surface a little towards the camera along the view ray, which keeps it on top of the terrain it lies on at any distance without shifting it on screen; a custom material has only [member height_offset] to keep it above the ground. The mesh's [code]UV.x[/code] runs from 0 at the left edge to 1 at the right one, and [code]UV.y[/code] along the spline, advancing by 1 every [member width] meters (both scaled by [member uv_scale]). The vertex color's alpha fades the edges and the ends out ([member edge_fade], [member end_fade_length]): for a [StandardMaterial3D], enable [member BaseMaterial3D.vertex_color_use_as_albedo] and a transparency mode to use it.

method.name: apply_preset
method.description: Sets [member spline_type] to [param type] and every property listed by [method get_preset] to that type's value.

method.name: apply_to_landscape
method.description: Shapes the [Landscape3D] to the spline. With [member carve_enabled], the ground across the strip is cut or filled to the curve's own height (following its tilt), [member carve_depth] further down along the middle for a river or stream bed, and blended back into the untouched terrain over [member carve_falloff] beyond the edges. With a valid [member paint_layer], that [TerrainLayer] is painted under the strip, fading out over [member paint_falloff]. The ground is shaped to the [i]curve's[/i] heights, not the terrain's, so place the curve's points on the ground first (with the Path3D tools' [b]Snap to Colliders[/b], the editor's [b]Snap Points to Terrain[/b], or [method project_to_landscape]). Only the terrain within reach of the spline is read or written (see [method get_landscape_footprint]), and the terrain's chunks, collision shape and textures are refreshed once for the whole edit. Applying again leaves the ground under the strip as it is, but eases the falloff a little further each time, since it blends with whatever the ground is. In the editor, the toolbar's [b]Apply to Landscape[/b] button does this as a single undoable action.

method.name: create_default_material
method.description: Returns a new copy of the built-in material a spline of this [param type] renders with when [member material] is empty, with its own copy of the shader, to assign to [member material] and adjust.

method.name: get_chunk_count
method.description: Returns how many chunks the strip is currently split into (see [member chunk_length]).

method.name: get_default_material
method.description: Returns the built-in material splines of this [param type] render with when [member material] is empty. It is shared by all of them; to change it for one spline, use [method create_default_material] instead.

method.name: get_landscape
method.description: Returns the [Landscape3D] this spline sits on: the target of [member landscape_path], or if that is empty, the nearest [Landscape3D] that is an ancestor of this node or a direct child of one of its ancestors. Returns [code]null[/code] if there is none, or while this node is outside the scene tree.

method.name: get_landscape_footprint
method.description: Returns the regions of the landscape's heightmap, in samples, that [method apply_to_landscape] reads and writes: blocks [constant Landscape3D.CHUNK_QUADS] samples on a side, only those the spline comes within reach of. Useful to snapshot the terrain before applying, for example with [method Landscape3D.get_height_regions].

method.name: get_preset
method.description: Returns the property values that suit a spline of this [param type], as a dictionary of property names to values: its width, [member height_mode], [member height_offset], how finely it is divided across, its fades, [member gi_mode], and how it carves and paints the landscape. The road preset matches the class's own default values.

method.name: project_to_landscape
method.description: Returns [param local_position] (in this node's local space) moved along the landscape's up axis onto its surface, matching the triangles the terrain actually renders. Returns [param local_position] unchanged if there is no landscape.

method.name: update_mesh
method.description: Brings the mesh up to date right away. Changes are otherwise gathered and applied once at the end of the frame, so this is only needed when something has to see the result within the same frame.

members.member: How far below the curve [method apply_to_landscape] digs the ground along the middle of the strip, in meters: [code]0[/code] for a road (the ground is flattened to the road's surface), the depth of the water for a river or stream. The bed is flat across the middle half of the width and rises to the curve's height at the edges.
If [code]true[/code], [method apply_to_landscape] shapes the ground's height to the spline. Turn it off to only paint [member paint_layer].

How far beyond each edge of the strip, in meters, [method apply_to_landscape] blends the shaped ground back into the untouched terrain: the embankments and cuttings along a road, or the banks of a river. The blend starts a terrain sample and a half ([member TerrainData.vertex_spacing] times 1.5) past the edge; the ground up to there is kept level with the edge, so the terrain triangles under the strip's edges are flat too.
Whether the strip casts shadows, as [member GeometryInstance3D.cast_shadow]. Off by default: lying on the ground, it has nothing to shadow.

The length along the spline, in meters, of each chunk the strip is split into. Each chunk is culled, chooses its level of detail and is rebuilt on its own, so shorter chunks cull and rebuild more precisely at the cost of more instances to draw.

How many segments the strip is divided into across its width. With [constant HEIGHT_MODE_CONFORM], this is how finely it follows the ground from side to side, so aim for about one segment per terrain sample across it. Columns the surface does not need are simplified away (see [member simplify_tolerance]), so level strips cost nothing extra for it.

How much of each side of the strip, as a fraction of its width, fades out towards the edge in the vertex color's alpha, so it blends into the ground instead of ending on a hard line. The built-in materials use it; see the class description for a [StandardMaterial3D].
How far from each end of an open spline, in meters, the vertex color's alpha fades out, so a river or stream peters out instead of stopping at a hard edge.
How the strip takes part in global illumination, as [member GeometryInstance3D.gi_mode].
Where the strip's surface is vertically. See [enum HeightMode]. Without a landscape, every mode follows the curve's own height.

How far the strip is lifted along the landscape's up axis, in meters: above the ground with [constant HEIGHT_MODE_CONFORM] and [constant HEIGHT_MODE_CONFORM_LEVEL] (keep it above the terrain's own level of detail changes, or the ground shows through in the distance), above the curve with [constant HEIGHT_MODE_SPLINE].
The [Landscape3D] to lay the strip on and to shape with [method apply_to_landscape]. If empty, the nearest one is found automatically (see [method get_landscape]).
Scales the distance at which each chunk switches to a coarser level of detail, as [member GeometryInstance3D.lod_bias].
The material the strip is rendered with. If empty, a built-in one for [member spline_type] is used (see [method get_default_material]).
How far beyond each edge of the strip, in meters, the painted [member paint_layer] fades out.
The index of the landscape's [TerrainLayer] that [method apply_to_landscape] paints under the strip, such as gravel under a road or mud along a river. [code]-1[/code] paints nothing.

The weight [member paint_layer] is raised to under the strip, from [code]0[/code] to [code]1[/code]. Painting only ever raises the layer to at least this weight (taking it from the other layers), so painting again changes nothing.
The render layers the strip is drawn on, as [member VisualInstance3D.layers].

How far apart, in meters, the spline is sampled into cross-sections before simplification. Smaller values follow tight bends and uneven ground more closely; straight, even stretches are simplified back down regardless (see [member simplify_tolerance]). With [constant HEIGHT_MODE_CONFORM] or [constant HEIGHT_MODE_CONFORM_LEVEL], keep it at or below the terrain's [member TerrainData.vertex_spacing] so the strip follows every bump in the ground.

How far, in meters, the simplified strip may stray from the full-detail one. Cross-sections and columns that lie within this distance of the surface their neighbors describe are left out of the mesh. [code]0[/code] keeps every one of them.

If [code]true[/code], curve points that have no handles of their own are joined smoothly, as if their handles pointed from the previous point towards the next one, instead of in straight lines meeting at a corner. Points given handles in the editor keep them.

What the spline is. It chooses the built-in material used while [member material] is empty; changing it in the Inspector also applies the matching preset to the other properties (see [method get_preset]), as a single undoable change. Setting it from a script changes only the type; use [method apply_preset] for the rest.
Scales the mesh's texture coordinates: [code]x[/code] across the strip (1 covers its width once), [code]y[/code] along it (1 repeats the texture once every [member width] meters).

The distance, in meters, beyond which a chunk is not drawn at all, as [member GeometryInstance3D.visibility_range_end]. Measured per chunk, so the near part of a long spline stays visible while the far part is skipped. [code]0[/code] draws it at any distance.
Over how many meters before [member visibility_range_end] a chunk fades out, instead of disappearing at once.
The width of the strip, in meters.
If set, scales [member width] along the spline: the curve's X axis runs from the spline's start (0) to its end (1), and its value multiplies the width there.

constants.constant: A road or path: drapes over the ground, and [method apply_to_landscape] flattens the ground under it.
A river: a level water surface that follows the curve's own height, and [method apply_to_landscape] digs its bed and banks.
A stream: narrow water that runs downhill with the ground, level across its width, in a shallow bed.
Represents the size of the [enum SplineType] enum.
Every vertex sits on the ground (plus [member height_offset]), across the width as well as along it. For roads and paths over uneven ground.

Follows the ground under the centerline along its length, but stays level across its width (banked by the curve's tilt). For streams, whose water runs downhill with the ground but whose surface is flat.
Follows the curve's own height and tilt, whatever the ground does. For rivers, whose surface has to stay level and smooth where the ground under it does not, and for anything raised off the ground.
